precepts.text: The accuser of our brethren is cast down, and they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb and the word of their testimony, and loved not their lives unto the death: in Jacob's trouble we do not fold, we do not spare our lives, and we are no traitors.
precepts.point: Be thou faithful unto death and I will give thee a crown of life: nothing they can take can make you betray eternal life, because there is no resurrection for them. He that hath an ear, let him hear; you have to keep the commandments to understand it, and he that overcometh is not hurt of the second death, the death over your soul.
precepts.why:
“Behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison, that ye may be tried; and ye shall have tribulation ten days”. They are going to pass laws to put us in prisons. That is why they keep building these detention facilities; they fill them with the people they call illegal aliens, but ultimately they are for the twelve tribes of Israel. Imagine ten days in a detention facility, being tortured, your wife and children or the brothers you war with slain in front of you, just to make you say you are not the twelve tribes and Christ is not black, and they will spare your life. Hell no. We have nothing to lose and everything to gain; they have no power over our souls.

Revelation 12 backs it up. We are going into Jacob’s trouble, when Esau does not want this gospel preached any further and will do whatever it takes to try to stop prophecy. “Now is come salvation, and strength, and the kingdom of our God, and the power of his Christ: for the accuser of our brethren is cast down, which accused them before our God day and night.” Our kingdom is soon to come; before then, we are accused day and night. That is the tribulation ten days, us losing our lives for this gospel.

“And they overcame him by the blood of the Lamb, and by the word of their testimony”. Their testimony is the testimony of this gospel. Even when persecution happens we will not fold; we don’t care about any white Jesus or any doctrine outside the twelve tribes of Israel being redeemed from our oppressors, Babylon America.

“And they loved not their lives unto the death.” We cannot be trying to spare our lives when Jacob’s trouble takes off. Loving not your life unto death means resisting every temptation to go against your God and your people. Don’t be a damn traitor. That is being faithful unto death for the crown of life.

precepts.text: Present your bodies a living sacrifice: every prophet who goes out to teach does, as John on Patmos and James beheaded did; we are the true martyrs.

precepts.why:
“Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee a crown of life.” This is what we are going to sacrifice to get what is actually ours: eternal life, the kingdom of heaven.

Paul says it: “I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that ye present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable unto God, which is your reasonable service.” Every time these prophets go out to teach the word, they are presenting their bodies a living sacrifice. All the prophets in the Bible did it, even unto death. John was banished to the isle of Patmos; James was beheaded. They were martyred because they understood the mission, and you brothers and sisters have to understand the mission. We are the true martyrs.

Many read “be thou faithful unto death” and do not understand it. You have to put yourself there and say: there is nothing these nations can do to me, nothing you can take from me, to make me turn and betray my eternal life. There is no resurrection for them.

“He that hath an ear, let him hear”: you have to be spiritual, keeping the commandments, to understand it. “He that overcometh shall not be hurt of the second death”, the death the Lord has power over, the death over your soul.

precepts.text: The ungodly, Esau, reason that life is short and no man returns from the grave. The righteous man was made to reprove their thoughts; he is grievous unto them even to behold, because we are a constant reminder that we are the sons of God and they are not. His life is not like other men's, his ways are of another fashion, and we are esteemed of him as counterfeits. God's own word calls them counterfeits, frauds, not the real Jews.

When that happens, we cannot help you; do not be in your feelings that nobody cares. Man up. That will be the case for some of us in here.

Wisdom of Solomon 2 lets you hear the synagogue of Satan think. “For the ungodly said, reasoning with themselves, but not aright, Our life is short and tedious, and in the death of a man there is no remedy: neither was there any man known to have returned from the grave.” This ungodly is Esau.

Now watch what Esau says about us. “He was made to reprove our thoughts.” The Israelite man, the prophet, was made to reprove their thoughts. “He is grievous unto us even to behold”: just looking at us grieves them, because we are a constant reminder that we are the sons of God and they are not. “For his life is not like other men’s, his ways are of another fashion”, because we keep the commandments of God.

“We are esteemed of him as counterfeits”. That goes to Revelation 2:9 and 3:9: they are counterfeits, fakes, frauds; they are not the real Jews. The Bible calls them counterfeits; those are not my words, those are the words of God. “He abstaineth from our ways as from filthiness: he pronounceth the end of the just to be blessed”.

So those which say they are Jews and are not know it themselves. The righteous man grieves them, and that is why the devil casts some of us into prison. Be faithful unto death.

precepts.text: Herod the king killed James with the sword and, seeing it pleased the Jews, took Peter also. The devil casting into prison was Rome and Herod, Satan's children.
precepts.point: When the Bible says devil, it is interchangeable: the father and his children. His children can do nothing without the spirit in them, the same way we can do nothing without the Lord in us.
precepts.why:
“Behold, the devil shall cast some of you into prison”. Did the literal devil come and cast people into prison? Did a spiritual demon snatch somebody and throw him in a cell? No. When the Bible says devil, it is interchangeable: it is talking about the father and his children. The same way we can do nothing without our Father and without the Lord in us, these people can do nothing without their father dwelling in them. He uses his children to do what he wants done.

Acts 12 shows who did it: “Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to vex certain of the church. And he killed James the brother of John with the sword. And because he saw it pleased the Jews, he proceeded further to take Peter also.” Herod was a white man, an Edomite. He killed James and put Peter in prison. So at that time the devil casting into prison was Herod, Satan’s children, Rome.

The seed of the devil came back as Esau, and the sons of God came back as Jacob: “I will put enmity between thee and the woman, and between thy seed and her seed”. Satan means adversary, accuser, opponent: he is the Lord’s adversary and ours, and so is his seed. Devil means deceiver: as he deceived Eve, his children deceive everyone on the earth. That is why we call the so-called white man the devil, because he deceives the whole earth, and Satan, because he is our adversary and God’s.

So know who we are fighting. This is war, and the devil still casts some of us into prison through his children.

precepts.point: Get rid of your own personal demonic sin before you line a brother up for his failure. In the furnace every evil thought and secret act against the congregation comes back.

The purpose of the wicked is to overthrow your goings. You think Satan is sleeping? There is the spiritual Satan and the physical Satan, and every time they are at work, they are working as a team. Whatever state you find yourself in, jail, about to be put to death, afflicted, tortured, losing an eye or an arm, be faithful, because pain is part of the walk. Mark 9 shows how that spirit works in us: “ofttimes it hath cast him into the fire, and into the waters, to destroy him”. That is us destroying ourselves in the club, the partying and religion, because Satan is in us and we thought it was the way. So pray to be kept from the hands of the wicked, and ask the Lord to strengthen your faith, because when your faith is weak, Satan keeps attacking you.

precepts.text: I know thy poverty, but thou art rich; and the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews and are not.
precepts.point: The merchandise of Babylon runs from gold and timber to slaves and souls of men. The countries of Israel are not underdeveloped but overexploited.

note.label: Raising Cain: The Son of Perdition, Merchants, and Captive Nations

precepts.why:
“I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich).” First and foremost, the riches are the promise of the kingdom of heaven. Unto us pertain the promises, the law, the adoption of sons, all of it; we are the ones Christ died for. That is the true riches.

But Revelation 18 gives it a new spin. Babylon trades in gold, silver, precious stones, fine wood, iron and marble, and these come out of our lands. So-called third world countries are rich with resources; it is the people who are poor, because they are overexploited. What a distinction. The countries of Israel are not underdeveloped, and the poverty of our people sits on top of the riches of our lands.

“and I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.” Those who say they are Jews and are not are part of the same machine working to oppress our people, and it is the same playbook of sanctions, isolation and regime change that runs through the whole system.

So Revelation 2:9 stands beside Revelation 18:12: the merchants of Babylon grow rich off the goods of the lands where Israel is scattered, while Israel lives in tribulation and poverty, though rich in the promises and in the land itself.

precepts.text: The blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.
precepts.point: Testifying today means naming them which say they are Jews and are not, and calling Edom the border of wickedness.

note.label: Judgement - the Testimony of the Two Witnesses

precepts.why:
John “bare record of the word of God, and of the testimony of Jesus Christ, and of all things that he saw.” He saw things and he wrote them down. The testimony is what God gave the prophets: to Moses, Isaiah, Jeremiah, Micah, Nahum, to Peter, Paul and the apostles. All the things these men wrote, the things that are going to happen to the children of Israel, is the testimony we as God’s witnesses are supposed to be speaking.

Here is one of those testimonies: “I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich)”. The real Jews are in a low state today. Then: “I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.”

That is what you are supposed to testify about. You have to identify the people that say they are Jews and are not, and say plainly: these people are not the people of God. Revelation 3:9 says it again: “Behold, I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie; behold, I will make them to come and worship before thy feet.”

When you read Revelation 2:9 and 3:9 on this earth, that is you testifying. We as God’s witnesses have to testify these things on the earth today.

precepts.text: The blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not.
precepts.point: God has heard their blasphemies against the mountains of Israel; when the whole earth rejoices, he will make Mount Seir desolate.
precepts.why:
Ezekiel 35:12 says God has heard all Edom’s blasphemies: “I have heard all thy blasphemies which thou hast spoken against the mountains of Israel, saying, They are laid desolate, they are given us to consume.” Christ names that same blasphemy in Revelation: “I know the blasphemy of them which say they are Jews, and are not, but are the synagogue of Satan.”

That is the blasphemy: Edom took over the land and said, it is given to us, we are the Jews. They are not the Jews, and the land is not theirs. Revelation 3:9 says it again: “I will make them of the synagogue of Satan, which say they are Jews, and are not, but do lie”. They are the devil the Bible speaks of, and it is the Son of God who said it.

The verse also speaks to our people: “I know thy works, and tribulation, and poverty, (but thou art rich)”. That is our poverty, but we are rich, because we are the children of God.

“Thus with your mouth ye have boasted against me, and have multiplied your words against me: I have heard them.” By calling themselves Jews and claiming the land as Jews, Edom has boasted against God, and God heard every word. So “When the whole earth rejoiceth, I will make thee desolate”: when all creation is singing, Edom is destroyed. “As thou didst rejoice at the inheritance of the house of Israel, because it was desolate, so will I do unto thee: thou shalt be desolate, O mount Seir, and all Idumea, even all of it”.

Our people share in the blasphemy too. Ezekiel 36:20 says that when Israel was scattered among the heathen “they profaned my holy name, when they said to them, These are the people of the Lord, and are gone forth out of his land.” Every black and Latino Christian who points at the people in the land and says, those are the Jews, profanes God’s name. It was prophesied that the Messiah would come through Edom’s religion, Christianity, as a lord bent on doing away with all moral restraints: keep no commandments, keep no laws. That is the religion of Edom, and Christ is its enemy.

precepts.text: He that overcometh receives power over the nations, to rule them with a rod of iron.
precepts.point: Israel are joint heirs, so the power over the nations given to Christ is given to them.

note.label: Pope Nicholas & the Moors of Spain

precepts.why:
In Psalms 2 the Father says to Christ, “Ask of me, and I shall give thee the heathen for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession. Thou shalt break them with a rod of iron; thou shalt dash them in pieces like a potter’s vessel.” Christ is going to inherit all these nations and rule the planet.

All that Christ was given, we share, because we are “joint-heirs with Christ”. That is what a joint heir is: what Christ gets, he is going to give to us. Here is the proof: “And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations: And he shall rule them with a rod of iron”.

This is what we read in Psalms 2 that Christ is going to get, but because we are joint heirs, we are going to get it too. “As the vessels of a potter shall they be broken to shivers: even as I received of my Father.” The same honor and glory the Father gave to Christ, Christ says, I am going to give you that same power.

All we have to do, brothers, is endure to the end. “If so be that we suffer with him, that we may be also glorified together”: he that overcometh and keepeth his works unto the end is the one who receives power over the nations.

precepts.text: No weapon formed against thee shall prosper, and every tongue against thee shall be condemned.
precepts.point: Israel must overcome its addictions and wait for that power, not act before its time.
precepts.why:
“And he that overcometh, and keepeth my works unto the end, to him will I give power over the nations.” Some do not understand what that power is going to give us, so Isaiah shows it. Read verse 16 first: “Behold, I have created the smith that bloweth the coals in the fire, and that bringeth forth an instrument for his work; and I have created the waster to destroy.” That is talking about the nuclear weapon.

Then: “No weapon that is formed against thee shall prosper.” Think about it: Esau shoots a nuclear weapon and you walk right through it. That is what you call power. When he says power, some of you have no idea what that means. That is power.

Can their weapons prosper against us today? Yes. That is why we must wait for that power. And it goes on: “and every tongue that shall rise against thee in judgment thou shalt condemn.” In that day, let me hear somebody rise against us with his tongue. I double dare you. Every tongue will be condemned.

“This is the heritage of the servants of the Lord, and their righteousness is of me, saith the Lord.” This is our heritage. We are the servants, and our righteousness is of the Most High.
